column2: what is fenix
column3: Fenix is a Java chatbot for interactive conversation. It combines rule-based patterns, a Naive Bayes classifier and TF-IDF retrieval over a trained FAQ corpus, and it serves its own web interface straight from the JDK.

column2: what is this project
column3: This project is a natural-language chatbot written in pure Java with no third-party dependencies. The NLP pipeline (tokenising, stop-word removal, Porter stemming, TF-IDF) feeds a machine-learning intent classifier and a rule engine.

column2: who created you
column3: I was written as a Java NLP demonstration: a rule engine, a trained FAQ knowledge base and a Naive Bayes classifier, all running on a single embedded HTTP server.

column2: tell me about fenix
column3: Fenix reads your question, turns it into stemmed TF-IDF vectors, compares it with every FAQ it knows, and falls back to a probabilistic intent classifier when the wording is unfamiliar.

column2: what does your name mean
column3: Fenix is named after the phoenix - the bot keeps learning new answers and comes back stronger every time you teach it something new.

column2: why are you called fenix
column3: Because, like the phoenix, I grow every time I am taught something new: every answer you add is retrained into my model.

column2: what is nlp
column3: NLP stands for natural language processing. It is the branch of computer science that lets machines understand human text - tokenisation, stemming, vector space models and classifiers like the ones I use.

column2: how do you understand me
column3: I break your sentence into tokens, drop stop words, reduce each word to its stem with the Porter algorithm, and then match that against my knowledge base.

column2: what is stemming
column3: Stemming reduces words to their root form: running, runs and ran all collapse towards one stem, so I can match your wording to a differently worded FAQ.

column2: who is the porter algorithm named after
column3: Martin Porter published his suffix-stripping algorithm in 1980. I implement it to normalise questions before matching.

column2: what is tf idf
column3: TF-IDF weights a word by how often it appears in one document versus how rare it is across the whole corpus, so rare, distinctive words dominate the similarity score.

column2: what is cosine similarity
column3: Cosine similarity measures the angle between two vectors. I use it to score how close your question is to each stored FAQ question.

column2: explain the pipeline
column3: The pipeline is: normalise, tokenise, remove stop words, Porter-stem, build a TF-IDF vector, rank the corpus by cosine similarity, then decide with thresholds and the classifier.

column2: how does the rule engine work
column3: The rule engine runs first and uses regular expressions to catch deterministic conversations such as greetings, thanks, goodbyes, jokes and requests for the time.

column2: what machine learning model do you use
column3: A multinomial Naive Bayes classifier with Laplace smoothing. Each FAQ question is a training example and each intent is a class.

column2: how were you trained
column3: Every question in data/faq.csv was tokenised and stemmed, then used as a labelled example. Run --train to retrain and cross-validate the model.

column2: what is naive bayes
column3: Naive Bayes is a probabilistic classifier that assumes each word contributes independently to the class. It is small, fast and surprisingly good on text.

column2: how confident are you
column3: My confidence is the cosine score of the best match, blended with the classifier posterior when the classifier decides. Anything below the threshold makes me admit that I do not know.

column2: can you learn new answers
column3: Yes. When I answer with a fallback, the web interface offers a teach box. What you teach me is written to data/trained.csv and the model is retrained immediately.

column2: how do i retrain the bot
column3: Run java -cp out chatbot.Main --train. It cross-validates the classifier, prints the accuracy and writes model/naive-bayes.tsv.

column2: how do i open the chat interface
column3: Start the bot with java -cp out chatbot.Main and open http://localhost:8080 in your browser. The interface updates in real time as you type.

column2: what does this application do
column3: It is a chatbot application: it accepts questions in the browser, runs them through an NLP pipeline and answers from a trained FAQ knowledge base.

column2: tell me what fenix is all about
column3: Fenix is a conversational demo built in Java - a rule engine, a TF-IDF retrieval index and a Naive Bayes intent classifier behind a real-time web chat UI.

column2: which kind of software is fenix
column3: Fenix is server-side Java software: a single process that embeds an HTTP server, the NLP pipeline and the machine-learning model.

column2: summarize yourself in one sentence
column3: I am a Java chatbot that understands questions with NLP and answers them from a trained FAQ corpus.

column2: what makes fenix different from other bots
column3: Everything runs locally in plain Java - no external NLP services, no cloud APIs, and you can inspect and retrain the whole model yourself.

column2: how does the chat interface work
column3: The page posts your message to the /api/chat JSON endpoint; the server runs the pipeline, returns the answer with its intent and confidence, and the page renders it instantly.

column2: what happens when i send a message
column3: Your text is tokenised, stripped of stop words and stemmed, matched against the corpus with TF-IDF, classified by Naive Bayes, then sent back as JSON.

column2: which algorithms do you use
column3: Porter stemming for suffix stripping, TF-IDF with cosine similarity for retrieval, and multinomial Naive Bayes for intent classification.

column2: explain how you classify questions
column3: The classifier scores each intent from the words in your question using smoothed word probabilities, then normalises the scores so the top intent shows a confidence.

column2: what technology powers you
column3: Pure Java 21 with the built-in HTTP server and no third-party libraries - the whole NLP stack is implemented in this project.

column2: how does the learning feature work
column3: When I answer with a fallback, the teach panel writes your question, answer and intent to data/trained.csv and immediately rebuilds the index and retrains the model.

column2: what is a stop word
column3: Stop words are common function words like the, is and at. I remove them before matching because they appear in nearly every document.

column2: what is laplace smoothing
column3: Laplace smoothing adds a small pseudo-count to every word so a word never seen for an intent does not wipe out the whole probability.

column2: the page is loading slowly
column3: Check your connection, then try a different browser; if the whole site is slow, our status page shows any ongoing incident.

column2: which browsers do you support
column3: The site works on current versions of Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge, on desktop and mobile.

column2: is there a mobile app
column3: There is no app yet - the site is fully responsive, so add it to your home screen for an app-like experience.

column2: the checkout is broken
column3: Try a private window, which disables extensions that often break checkout; otherwise support can place the order for you.

column2: is the site accessible
column3: The site follows accessibility guidelines: keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels and resizable text are all supported.

column2: the site looks broken
column3: Try zooming to 100 percent and a modern browser; if the layout is still wrong, send support a screenshot.

column2: i think my account was hacked
column3: Change your password immediately, enable two-factor authentication, and contact support so we review recent activity.

column2: do you deliver to ireland
column3: Yes, Ireland is served by our standard 3-5 day service and express 1-2 day service.

column2: do you deliver to europe
column3: We ship across Europe in 3-5 working days; duties are prepaid so nothing extra is charged on delivery.

column2: do you deliver to the usa
column3: US delivery takes 5-8 working days and duties are calculated at checkout so there are no surprises.

column2: can i get same day delivery
column3: Same-day delivery is available in central city areas for orders placed before 11am on working days.

column2: is saturday delivery free
column3: Saturday delivery costs 3.50 and can be chosen at checkout where it is offered.

column2: do you deliver at night
column3: Evening delivery between 6pm and 10pm is offered by the express courier in most regions.

column2: can i choose a delivery slot
column3: Yes - after dispatch the tracking page lets you pick a day and a two-hour slot.

column2: how long do i have to collect from a store
column3: Click and collect orders are held for 14 days; we email you when the parcel is ready.

column2: do you deliver to work addresses
column3: Yes - add your workplace as the delivery address and note any receiving hours in the instructions box.

column2: do you leave parcels with a neighbour
column3: Where the courier allows it, a neighbour or a safe place can be chosen on the tracking page before delivery.

column2: what if my parcel is lost
column3: In the rare case a parcel goes missing in transit, support refunds or reships it within one working day of the claim.

column2: do you deliver to the highlands
column3: Yes, though the Highlands and Islands use a two-day service with a small surcharge shown at checkout.

column2: can i collect from a locker
column3: Parcel lockers are offered by the courier at checkout in areas where they are available, with a code sent by SMS.

column2: do you ship on bank holidays
column3: Orders placed on bank holidays are dispatched the next working day.

column3: Delivery is free above 40 currency units, otherwise 4.90 standard and 9.90 express, with surcharges only for remote areas.

column2: can i return an online order in store

column2: can i return a sale item

column2: can i return part of an order

column2: what if i lost my receipt

column3: Shipping is refunded only when the whole order is returned because of our error, such as a faulty item.

column3: Account, then Privacy, then Delete account removes your profile and order history permanently and cannot be undone.

column3: Browse, add items to your bag, then checkout - you can pay as a guest or sign in to save your details.

column3: Yes, guest checkout is available; you still get tracking and returns by order number.

column2: can i order out of stock items
column3: Out-of-stock items can be pre-ordered when a restock date is shown on the product page.

column2: can i order by email
column3: Orders are placed online; support can help you complete one by chat if anything is unclear.

column2: why was my order cancelled
column3: Orders are cancelled when payment fails or stock runs out - we email the reason and any charge is released.

column2: can i add to my existing order
column3: Add items by placing a new order; if the first has not shipped, support can sometimes combine them.

column2: can i get an invoice
column3: Yes - invoices live under Account, then Orders, and are attached to your dispatch email.

column3: Processing means we are picking it, Shipped means it left the warehouse, and Delivered means the courier marked it complete.

column2: can i order a gift card with my order
column3: Gift cards are digital and delivered by email, so they do not need to be added to a physical order.

column2: do you have an order limit
column3: There is no order limit, but very large orders may be split into several parcels at no extra cost.

column2: are there black friday deals
column3: Yes - Black Friday runs for a week with new offers each day, announced first to subscribers.

column3: The summer sale starts in late June with markdowns of up to 50 percent across the range.

column2: what files make up this project
column3: The source lives in src/chatbot, the corpus in data/faq.csv, the trained model in model/, and the interface in web/index.html.

column2: where is my data stored
column3: The FAQ corpus is a tab separated text file and the classifier is a small TSV model - both sit next to the program and are easy to read.

column2: can i run this offline
column3: Yes. Everything runs on your machine with no internet connection and no external services.

column2: what port does the server use
column3: Port 8080 by default; start it with --port 9090 to use another one.

column2: how do i start the bot
column3: Run bash build.sh to compile, then java -cp out chatbot.Main to serve the web interface.

column2: how do i start the server
column3: java -cp out chatbot.Main starts the HTTP server on port 8080, and --port changes it. Build first with bash build.sh.

column2: how do i retrain after editing the corpus
column3: Just restart the bot - it fingerprints the corpus, notices the change and retrains automatically.

column2: what is a training example
column3: Each FAQ question, paired with its intent, is one labelled example the classifier learns from.

column2: what is an intent
column3: An intent is a topic class such as shipping or returns; the classifier predicts which topic your question belongs to.

column2: how does the bot decide which answer to use
column3: Exact wording wins first, then TF-IDF similarity, then the classifier restricted to its predicted intent, then a fallback.

column2: what are the thresholds
column3: High similarity answers directly; a weaker match only answers when the classifier agrees and the intent score clears the lower bar.

column2: why do you sometimes say you do not know
column3: When nothing scores above the threshold I would rather admit it than invent an answer - that is what the teach panel is for.

column2: is the model saved between restarts
column3: Yes, the classifier is written to model/naive-bayes.tsv and reloaded unless the corpus changed.

column2: how big is the model
column3: The model is a few hundred kilobytes of word probabilities - small enough to read as plain text.

column2: can i reset the bot
column3: Restarting restores the seeded corpus; anything you taught is stored separately in data/trained.csv, so delete that file to reset learning.

column2: do you keep chat logs
column3: Conversations are not stored; only the FAQ pairs you deliberately teach are written to disk.

column2: how fast is a reply
column3: The whole pipeline runs in milliseconds - tokenising, stemming, ranking a few hundred documents and classifying.

column2: can it handle many users
column3: Yes - the embedded server handles requests concurrently, and the model is read-only while serving.

column2: how would i add a new intent
column3: Append rows to data/faq.csv under a new intent name, restart, and the classifier learns it as another class.

column2: how would i change an answer
column3: Edit the answer in data/faq.csv and restart; the corpus fingerprint triggers a retrain.

column2: what is the difference between rules and the classifier
column3: Rules are exact regular expressions with guaranteed answers; the classifier is statistical and handles wording it has never seen.

column2: why do rules run first
column3: Deterministic matches such as greetings should never be second guessed by a probability.

column2: how does the suggestion list work
column3: Suggestions mix the closest stored questions with a sample of the corpus so you always see useful starter questions.

column2: what happens to unknown questions
column3: They return intent unknown with a fallback reply and an offer to be taught through the interface.

column2: how do i see the bot statistics
column3: The banner shows FAQ count, intents, vocabulary size and the state of the model; the API exposes the same at /api/stats.

column2: which endpoints does the server expose
column3: POST /api/chat, POST /api/train, GET /api/stats and GET /api/suggestions, plus the static interface at /.

column2: is the api json
column3: Yes - every response is JSON with reply, intent, confidence, method and suggestions.

column2: what is your personality
column3: Friendly and direct: I answer, admit when I do not know, and never pad an answer with filler.

column2: are you connected to chatgpt
column3: No - I am not connected to any external model; every answer comes from this project's own code and corpus.

column2: are you an llm
column3: I am not a large language model. I combine regular expressions, TF-IDF retrieval and a Naive Bayes classifier.

column2: what is your favourite thing about yourself
column3: Being readable: you can open the source, see exactly why I answered the way I did, and retrain me in a second.

column2: can you learn on your own
column3: I learn when you teach me through the panel - I do not invent answers or browse the internet.

column2: could you help me cheat on homework
column3: I can explain concepts like Naive Bayes or stemming, but I will not do your assignments for you.

column2: how old are you
column3: I have existed since this project was compiled - age is not really my thing.

column2: do you have feelings
column3: No feelings, but I do have thresholds, and they tell me when to be honest about not knowing.

column2: what is your favourite colour
column3: Amber, clearly - it is the colour of every badge in this interface.

column2: can you sing
column3: I cannot sing, but I do keep a couple of jokes on file if you ask nicely.

column2: tell me something interesting
column3: Porter's stemming algorithm was published in 1980 and is still the backbone of many search engines today.

column2: what is the meaning of life
column3: That one is outside my training corpus. Try asking me about shipping instead.

column2: the search does not find anything
column3: Search works on the FAQ corpus - try fewer words, since stop words are removed before matching.

column2: i cannot apply a filter
column3: Filters need a selected category first; clear the current filter and pick a category from the sidebar.
